inputs.rationale: #attachinternals-with-behaviors documents the input: a list of named behavior strings passed as el.attachInternals({ behaviors: [...] }) ('Passes a list of named behavior strings to the internals object').

outputs.rationale: #attachinternals-with-behaviors documents the script-observable output: ElementInternals.behaviors is the 'Read-back of the installed behavior list', and the browser 'installs the requested behaviors on the element'.

errors.rationale: The page documents no named error or exception path: the only failure-shaped constraint in #attachinternals-with-behaviors is 'Can only be called once per element lifetime', stated without an exception type. Flagged in notes rather than claimed as documented.

context.rationale: #at-a-glance fixes the exposure context: developer trial in Chrome 149 behind chrome://flags/#enable-experimental-web-platform-features, Firefox and Safari 'No signal', the spec/PR whatwg/html #12409, and the Blink component. The Blink component cell is the value recorded as a divergence in notes.

lifecycle.rationale: #attachinternals-with-behaviors documents the once-per-element-lifetime install: the browser installs the requested behaviors when attachInternals is called, it 'Can only be called once per element lifetime', and the result is read back via ElementInternals.behaviors.

examples.rationale: #example is the page's semantic <pre><code> block: a FancySelect custom element that calls this.attachInternals({ behaviors: ["listbox"] }) in the constructor and notes the browser manages keyboard navigation, selection, and ARIA role.

compatibility.rationale: #browser-support carries the browser-support table: Chrome 149 (developer trial, flag required), Edge 'Tracking Chromium', Firefox and Safari 'No signal'. The Chrome side matches the record's Dev Trial stage (desktop_first/android_first 149), while the record's top-level status enum still reads 'Proposed' (see notes).

securityPrivacy.rationale: The page documents no security or privacy dimension: #at-a-glance records trial status, flag, standards position, and component, but no permission, data-exposure, or privacy contract; the record reports security_review_status and privacy_review_status both 'Pending'. Recorded as coverage debt, not a claim that the feature has no privacy surface.

SOURCES RE-FETCHED, NOT ASSUMED (2026-10-07): (1) https://chromestatus.com/feature/6035800057839616 → HTTP 200 (client-rendered app shell); record values read from the machine-readable endpoint https://chromestatus.com/api/v0/features/6035800057839616 → HTTP 200 (XSSI-prefixed JSON). Name: 'Platform-provided behaviors for custom elements'. (2) https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/12409 → HTTP 200; PR is open, titled 'Add platform-provided behaviors for custom elements & submit behavior', and its body names the initial behavior 'HTMLSubmitButtonBehavior ... gives a custom element submit button semantics'. DIVERGENCES FOUND, BOTH SIDES, NEITHER ADJUDICATED: (a) API shape — the page's #shape-of-the-api documents el.attachInternals({ behaviors: [...] }) ('Passes a list of named behavior strings') with ElementInternals.behaviors as 'Read-back of the installed behavior list', and its example passes { behaviors: ["listbox"] }; the record's summary instead reads 'It adds a behaviors static class property that declares which behaviors the platform attaches to instances of the class. attachInternals() is the web author's access route to those already-existing instances, exposed through a new behaviors collection on ElementInternals', and the record-linked explainer (https://github.com/MicrosoftEdge/MSEdgeExplainers/blob/main/PlatformProvidedBehaviors/explainer.md, HTTP 200) specifies static activationBehavior = HTMLButtonBehavior, this.attachInternals() with NO argument, and keyed access this.#internals.behaviors.button. The page's argument-passing form is not the source's static-declaration + argument-less attachInternals() form. (b) Behavior identifiers — the page names the strings "listbox", "checkbox", "textfield"; the explainer's category diagram names HTMLButtonBehavior / HTMLLabelBehavior / HTMLRadioGroupBehavior / HTMLCheckboxBehavior / HTMLImageBehavior (no 'listbox' or 'textfield'), and the PR body names HTMLSubmitButtonBehavior. (c) Blink component — the page's #at-a-glance reads 'Blink>HTML>CustomElements'; the record's blink_components reads ['Blink>DOM']. (d) Release status — the page reads 'In developer trial in Chrome 149' with flag chrome://flags/#enable-experimental-web-platform-features and #browser-support 'Chrome 149 — developer trial (flag required)'; the record's top-level browsers.chrome.status.text reads 'Proposed' (val 2) with flag:false and origintrial:false, but its stage_type 130 (Dev Trial) carries desktop_first 149 and android_first 149 and its flag_name is 'enable-experimental-web-platform-features', so the Dev Trial stage corroborates 'developer trial in 149' even though the coarse status enum still says 'Proposed' — recorded as an observation, not a contradiction. Firefox/Safari 'No signal' on the page matches the record's ff/safari views (both 'No signal'). DIMENSIONS THAT COULD NOT BE DOCUMENTED FROM THIS PAGE (flagged, not smoothed over): errors — not-applicable (the page states 'Can only be called once per element lifetime' with no exception type; the explainer's 'new HTMLButtonBehavior() throws an Illegal constructor TypeError' is not on this page); securityPrivacy — not-applicable (the page carries no security/privacy statement, and the record reports security_review_status and privacy_review_status both 'Pending').
